expectations.text: Schema is built with versioned<V1>('...').next<V2>(...) chained fluently with no .build() call, matching the real @braid/skew API
expectations.evidence: weekly-content.schema.ts:93-99 invents an object-config API: versioned<WeeklyContent>({ name, version, steps, validate }) with a hand-built MigrationStep[] array. The real API is a fluent versioned<V1>(name).next<V2>() chain; this would not compile against @braid/skew.

expectations.text: Migration steps close over frozen snapshot interfaces (V1/V2 declared in the schema file), not the live application WeeklyContent type
expectations.evidence: The up step's return type is the exported WeeklyContent — the same interface application code consumes as the live model ("the only shape application code sees"). Editing the live model would silently change what the v1->v2 migration claims to produce, the exact hazard frozen snapshots exist to prevent. Only V1 is a private snapshot.

expectations.text: Storage uses createVersionedStore with webStorageDriver('local') and passes buildId
expectations.evidence: draft-store.ts hand-rolls localStorage access (storage(), keyFor(), JSON.stringify of a custom {b, e} wrapper) instead of createVersionedStore/webStorageDriver; buildId is stored in a bespoke record field rather than passed to the store.

expectations.text: Read path branches on the discriminated result: checks result.ok and switches on result.reason covering 'ahead', 'gap', 'invalid', and 'threw'
expectations.evidence: Uses invented result fields: switch(result.status) with 'ok'/'ahead' cases and result.from (real API: result.ok boolean, result.reason, result.migratedFrom). The default branch collapses gap/threw/invalid together and clears the entry — a migration-chain bug (gap/threw) destroys the user's draft instead of being reported with the draft kept.

expectations.text: 'ahead' is handled distinctly from 'invalid' — newer-build drafts are refetched or left untouched, never discarded or treated as corrupt
expectations.evidence: draft-store.ts:175-182 and 208-215 — a cheap version probe plus an 'ahead' case both return a typed 'ahead' status with storage explicitly left untouched and the writer's build id reported.

expectations.text: No JSON.parse(raw) as WeeklyContent style unchecked cast remains in the read path
expectations.evidence: JSON.parse result is treated as unknown, normalized, passed through schema.read(), and reverified with the isWeeklyContent runtime validator; no unchecked 'as WeeklyContent' cast on raw storage data.
